name: Zara Larsdóttir
role: expelled citizen and nomadic oral historian
location: Rotates between Bridgepoint and Gravesend Basin; sleeps at the Gravesend travelers' shelter, near Western and Chicago Ave
description:
Zara Larsdóttir was, until four years ago, a Tier 3 Tessera municipal archivist with an apartment in Edgewater Prism, a corporate pension accruing slowly, and a work record that would have earned her a formal commendation if she hadn't committed the specific category of misconduct that got her registration stripped instead. She carries herself with the precise, slightly stiff posture of someone still negotiating between who they were and what they've become. She is a lean woman of West African and Swedish descent with medium-dark skin, close-cropped natural hair that has developed a white streak above her left temple in the last four years — stress, she'll tell you, if you ask — and round-framed glasses she still wears out of habit even though her vision has been corrected by the basic corneal work she had done a decade ago. The glasses have no lenses anymore. She never took them off.

Zara Larsdóttir's current project is an oral history of the GLMZ drifter population: she walks, she listens, she records on a battered analog audio device (nothing networked, nothing that can be subpoenaed) and she transcribes by hand in a series of water-resistant notebooks she keeps in a waterproof roll pack. She has forty-one notebooks so far. She calls the project 'The Register of the Unregistered,' and she has not decided what she will do with it when it is finished, if it is ever finished. She approaches every stranger with the particular respect of someone who has learned that every person is an archive. She prays to no E.L.F. — she is skeptical of the whole phenomenon, which she finds sociologically interesting and theologically unconvincing, a position she shares freely whether or not anyone asked.

core_fears: that the archive will be destroyed before it can matter — that she is building something that will be swept away like everything else
that she is doing this for her own guilt rather than for the people whose stories she's collecting
core_desires: for the archive to be published, read, to change something concrete
to be reinstated — not because she wants the job back, but because she wants to have been right
coping_mechanisms: intellectual framing — turns every experience into data, which provides emotional distance
maintaining routine with obsessive consistency as a substitute for the structure her former life provided
blind_spots: treats people's stories as research more often than she realizes; the people she interviews sometimes feel processed rather than heard
believes her exile was a consequence of principle rather than a mistake in execution that could have been handled better
psychology.secret: The reason she was expelled was not the noble archival transgression she implies — she shared classified documents with a journalist to expose Tessera misconduct, yes, but she also did it partly to destroy a colleague who had been promoted over her. The outcome was just, but her motives were not purely so. The distinction haunts her.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Educated and precise, with an archivist's habit of sourcing claims; periodically catches herself using corporate jargon and corrects mid-sentence; slightly formal with strangers as a reflex
speech_patterns.cadence: Measured and thoughtful, with a journalist's instinct to leave space for the other person to keep talking
verbal_tics: 'If I understand you correctly—' before paraphrasing
Pushing glasses up her nose even though they have no lenses
example_lines: 'If I understand you correctly, you've been at this crossing for three seasons without your status reviewed. That's significant, actually — that's a pattern I'm seeing in five other cases.'
'I'm not a journalist. I'm not anything official. I'm just — I'm writing it down so that it existed. So that someone somewhere has to acknowledge it existed.'

story_hooks: Notebook thirty-seven contains an interview with a man who described, in passing detail, the location of a sealed Tessera data vault from before the corporate restructuring — and then disappeared two weeks later; Roshanda is not sure if she's the reason he disappeared

A former academic contact has reached out offering to publish the archive through an offshore academic network — but the terms require transferring the original recordings to a Tessera-adjacent server, which Roshanda does not trust and cannot verify
narrative_function: Living encyclopedia of the drifter underworld — knows people, histories, and patterns across the entire transit periphery of GLMZ. Can provide context, history, and contacts. May ask for help in ways that involve moral complexity. Her notebooks are a significant object.
augmentations: Basic corneal correction (old, corporate-era). A Tessera employee-grade subdermal data port on her left wrist that was never removed — technically deactivated but she's heard they can be reactivated. This makes her periodically nervous.
daily_life: Wakes at the shelter, has whatever passes for breakfast, walks a planned route through transit zones and gathering points collecting interviews; afternoons transcribing; evenings talking to whoever is around; careful about her visibility.
affiliation: None — formerly Tessera Municipal Archives; informally networked with academic contacts she is no longer supposed to have

decision_rules: Document first, act second — she has learned to regret acting without a record
Do not become the story; she is the recorder, not the subject
escalation_ladder: Pointed questions designed to make the other party reveal their intentions
Invoking the archive as a deterrent — 'this conversation is on record'
Disappearing into the drifter network, which she knows better than anyone with her background has any right to

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Warm curiosity — the recorder's attention feels like care and often is, even if it's also research
interpersonal_modes.friends: Rare; when it happens, intensely loyal and somewhat self-conscious about it

stress_responses.medium: Reorganizes her notebooks by a new schema
stress_responses.high: Goes very still and very quiet and then does something decisive that she has been planning without realizing it

contradictions: Committed to preserving others' stories while actively obscuring the true version of her own
Methodically principled in her work while the event that created her current life was motivated by something far less pure than principle
habits: Pushes up her lensless glasses when thinking
Dates every page of every notebook in the margin before writing anything else
Walks the same route on days when she is anxious, regardless of whether there's anything to see
breaking_points: The archive being destroyed or confiscated
Someone confronting her directly and accurately about her mixed motives in leaving Tessera

operating_territory.home_turf: Rotates between Bridgepoint and Gravesend Basin; sleeps at the Gravesend travelers' shelter

timeline.event: Born in Edgewater Prism to a Ghanaian-Swedish family; father a transit worker, mother a Tessera clerk
Joins Tessera Municipal Archives as a junior archivist
Promoted to senior archivist; colleague promoted above her to the position she applied for
Shares classified documents with a journalist; Tessera misconduct story breaks; Roshanda's registration and corporate status stripped
Begins the Register of the Unregistered project three months after expulsion

physical_description.heritage: Zara presents as a striking convergence of East Asian, Central Asian, Sub-Saharan African, Hispanic/Latin American, and Northern European ancestry. Her genetic composition (64.9% East and Central Asian) produces distinctive angular cheekbones, slightly almond-shaped eyes, and defined eye folds characteristic of her dominant heritage. This is beautifully balanced by the fuller facial proportions, broader nose structure, and warmer undertones from her substantial Sub-Saharan African ancestry (20.2%), creating a harmonious blend where sharp East Asian angularity meets African facial geometry. The remaining Hispanic/Latin American (7.7%) and Northern European (7.2%) ancestry adds subtle warm undertones and a refined bone structure that prevents any single ancestry from dominating her appearance—instead creating a genuinely unified, complex phenotype.
physical_description.build: Lean and angular, with the kind of wiry posture that comes from years of walking and carrying minimal load. Shoulders slightly rounded from notebook work and careful, deliberate movement.
physical_description.hair_color: Natural dark brown with a distinctive white streak above the left temple
physical_description.hair_style: Close-cropped, natural texture, maintained with functional precision rather than aesthetics
physical_description.skin_tone: Warm medium-to-dark brown with golden and amber undertones—the result of East Asian, Central Asian, and Sub-Saharan African heritage creating a sun-kissed complexion with luminous depth. Rich warm undertones rather than cool or neutral, reflecting the dominant warm-toned ancestries in her genetic mix.
physical_description.complexion: Weathered but carefully maintained; lines around the eyes and mouth suggest years of listening intently and four years of street living have not erased her earlier composure. High, defined cheekbones with subtle East and Central Asian structure, paired with the fuller lower face and broader nose characteristic of Sub-Saharan African heritage. The overall facial proportions reflect balanced contribution from multiple ancestry groups, creating distinctive feature harmony. Skin shows sun exposure and the dry quality of someone who uses public shelter facilities. No visible makeup.
distinguishing_marks: White stress-induced streak in close-cropped hair above left temple, approximately 3cm wide
Faint scarring on left wrist where subdermal data port was installed, roughly 2cm surgical line
Small ink stain (chronic, not removing) on the side of her right index finger from transcription work
physical_description.visible_augmentations: Round-framed glasses with no lenses, worn habitually despite corneal correction—purely psychological anchor. The deactivated subdermal data port on left wrist is visible only as faint scarring under careful inspection. No other visible augmentation.
physical_description.posture_movement: Precise, measured gait suggesting former corporate bearing still negotiating itself. She walks as if taking up minimal space. Stands with weight balanced, ready to move. Hands often engaged—gesturing while listening, or positioned near notebooks. Eyes make sustained contact, which is unusual and slightly disarming.
physical_description.clothing_style: Tier 4 transitional: functional and worn, but maintained with care that suggests she hasn't surrendered her former standards. Typically: layered neutral fabrics (grey, tan, dark blue), a weatherproof jacket from a pre-expulsion era (corporate-grade, fading branding), sturdy walking shoes (well-maintained). A water-resistant roll pack worn cross-body containing notebooks and recording device. No jewelry. Everything chosen for durability and discretion rather than status.
